hook: You're not too sensitive. You just never had a name for what you were picking up.
body:
**You're not too sensitive. You just never had a name for what you were picking up.**

There's a particular kind of exhaustion that comes from spending your whole life noticing things and then having to convince yourself that what you noticed wasn't real. That conversation where something felt slightly off. That person who seemed kind but left you feeling subtly drained every time. That relationship that looked fine from the outside but quietly cost you something.

You felt all of it. And then you were told — or you told yourself — that you were reading too much into things.

Here's what's actually true: the capacity to pick up on subtle emotional signals is not a flaw. It is a skill. The problem isn't that you feel too much. The problem is that nobody ever taught you how to interpret what you feel — so it just circles as anxiety instead of landing as information.

Sensitivity without a framework becomes noise. Sensitivity with a framework becomes your clearest tool in any relationship.

The next time you feel that low-grade unease after an interaction — don't dismiss it and don't spiral. Just ask yourself: what specifically triggered this feeling? Get it to one concrete observation. That's the beginning of turning a feeling into a read.

Full guide is in my bio if you want the whole system.
